newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mosenergo jumps as most Russian shares ease.
newsitem.headline: Mosenergo jumps as most Russian shares ease.

text.p: Most leading Russian shares edged down on Thursday but power utility Mosenergo firmed through the day on rumours company moves to limit shareholder voting rights would fail, traders said.

After the market closed, Mosenergo announced that it had dropped proposals to limit voting rights for major shareholders and an authorised capital expansion slated for the annual meeting on Monday. Traders speculated on the decisions all day.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares edged down 1.25 percent to 295.08 on $27.78 million total market volume.
National utility UES slipped to $0.2185 from $0.2188 and oil producer LUKoil edged up to $13.60 from $13.58.
But Mosenergo, accounting for most of the market's turnover, rose to $1.295 from $1.213 at Wednesday's close.
Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin said traders had bet the proposal to limit shareholder voting rights would fail and the authorised share increase would pass.
But operators said the West had not bought.

"I did not see clients' interest in buying Mosenergo today," said UCB chief trader Samit Yakovlev. "And the crazy volume means nothing -- it is not about clients' money, but about the same 150 shares changing hands many times."
Galperin forecast rejection of the proposals would lift the entire market.
But Yakovlev said that before big clients appeared on the market, it would only fluctuate.
"With the exception of Mosenergo, I cannot see clients interested in Russia, that's why the same fluctuation may continue tomorrow," he said.
